These ten hypotheses come from patterns in the 100 experiments. Each rests on a few parent cells, so they are weak evidence for the general case.

- **Edge 5 to `nor_conv_3x3` (rows 11-15 vs 16-20):** the gain is large when edge 5 was `avg_pool_3x3` (+3 to +9 points). It is near zero when edge 5 was `nor_conv_1x1`. When edge 3 is `nor_conv_1x1` the gain is also larger than when edge 3 is `skip_connect`.
- **Edge 3 to `skip_connect` (rows 26-30):** the effect is mostly positive when edge 3 was `nor_conv_3x3`.
- **Edge 3 to `nor_conv_3x3` (rows 66-70):** the effect is consistently negative when edge 3 was `skip_connect`.
- **Edge 0 to `none` (rows 71-80):** this edit is least harmful when edge 1 is `nor_conv_3x3`. It is catastrophic when edge 1 is `none` (-13.7 and -17.1 points on ImageNet16-120).
- **Edge 2 to `nor_conv_3x3` (rows 51-55 vs 56-60):** the gains are positive on all datasets when edge 2 was `skip_connect`, and near zero when it was `nor_conv_1x1`.
- **Edge 5 to `skip_connect` (rows 81-85):** this is more harmful when edge 5 was `nor_conv_3x3`.
- **Edge 0 to `nor_conv_3x3` (rows 5, 10):** C100 and IN16 both improved when edge 3 was `avg_pool_3x3`, while the `none` parent was clearly negative.
- **Edge 4 to `nor_conv_3x3` (rows 46-50):** all five gains are positive on all three datasets when edge 3 is `skip_connect`.
